builds.name: Reference: Ranked support core
builds.goal: Reference for Maokai: the core and runes ranked Emerald+ support players use most (385 ranked Emerald+ games with this core on OP.GG, patch 16.20, 59.7% win rate).
builds.hypothesis: A durable controller who starts fights with a targeted root, pushes enemies with Q and recovers through repeated Sap Magic attacks. The current support provider core anchors this plan; later slots are observed options or reviewed kit completions. Core in purchase order: Locket of the Iron Solari → Bandlepipes → Thornmail. Aftershock keystone as played in those games. Remaining slots: Boots of Swiftness, Celestial Opposition, Knight's Vow.
builds.summary: The proven support baseline: Locket of the Iron Solari → Bandlepipes → Thornmail, with Aftershock.
testPlan: Play it in support as your control build. Follow the purchase order; the core (Locket of the Iron Solari → Bandlepipes → Thornmail) is what ranked players complete first.
Record kills, deaths, damage dealt and the minute you finish each core item, then compare other builds against these numbers in similar games.
Adapt the last two items to the enemy team: armor or magic resist against fed carries, anti-heal against healing, penetration once enemies stack resists.
failureConditions: Your results with this build fall clearly below the 59.7% ranked baseline over several games in the same role.
The enemy team composition makes the core items poor answers; swap the flexible slots before abandoning the core.
tradeoffs: Proven and predictable, so opponents know what to expect. It is a starting point, not the best build for every matchup.
The observed core and individual options do not establish six-item build statistics. Late slots are kit-based inferences.
Six-slot completion is our kit-based inference, not an observed six-item win-rate build.  Situational options replace an appropriate slot; they are not added as a seventh item.
buyOrder: Core in purchase order: Locket of the Iron Solari → Bandlepipes → Thornmail.
Boots after the first item unless the lane needs them earlier.
coverageNotes: Source: OP.GG ranked Emerald+ solo/duo, patch 16.20, checked 2026-10-14. Core items and rune page are observed; later slots are observed options or reviewed completions. Win rates describe those games, not a prediction for yours.

Using an Ability or being hit by an enemy champion's Ability reduces the Cooldown by [4] seconds. Being hit by large or epic monster's Attacks or Abilities reduces the Cooldown by [1.5] second.

Maokai summons a colossal wave of brambles and thorns, Rooting enemies for [0.75] to [2.25] seconds, increasing with distance travelled, and dealing [150 / 225 / 300 + (0.75) × AP] magic damage. Hitting a champion gives Maokai [(0.4 / 0.5 / 0.6) × 100]% Move Speed, decaying over [2] seconds.

Maokai smashes his fist into the ground, dealing [75 / 120 / 165 / 210 / 255 + (0.5) × AP] plus [(0.02 / 0.025 / 0.03 / 0.035 / 0.04) × 100]% max Health magic damage and briefly Slowing. Nearby enemies are also Knocked Back.

Maokai transforms into a moving mass of roots, becoming Untargetable and dashing to an enemy. Upon arrival, he Roots the enemy for [1 / 1.1 / 1.2 / 1.3 / 1.4] second(s) and deals [60 / 85 / 110 / 135 / 160 + (0.4) × AP] magic damage.

Maokai flings a sapling, which stands watch for [30] seconds. Saplings chase nearby enemies, detonating on arrival to deal [50 / 75 / 100 / 125 / 150 + (0.25) × AP + (0.05) × Stat(12)[statFormula=2]] magic damage and Slow surrounding enemies by [45]% for [2] seconds. Sap Magic's Cooldown is reduced by an additional 4 seconds if the sapling hits an enemy champion or epic monster.

If placed in brush, Saplings instead last for [30 + (0.015) × Stat(12)[statFormula=2]] seconds and cause a larger explosion, dealing [100 / 150 / 200 / 250 / 300 + (0.5) × AP + (0.1) × Stat(12)[statFormula=2]] magic damage over [2] seconds and Slowing enemies by [0.45 + (0.0001) × AP + ((0.01) × (0.01)) × Stat(12)[statFormula=2]].

builds.name: Brush Health Ap Zone
builds.summary: Compare brush and non-brush E damage and lifetime.
builds.goal: Compare brush and non-brush E damage and lifetime.
builds.hypothesis: E brush saplings double documented base/AP/health damage and gain health-scaled duration plus AP/health slow. Earned Heartsteel health and Riftmaker conversion can support E while Blackfire tests two-second damage persistence; Q/W maintain access for a follow-up.
testPlan: Required state: Place E in brush with finite earned health and champion contact.
Compare brush and non-brush E damage and lifetime; repeat at equal gold, finite stacks, same ranks and defenses against a moving target.

Run three trials at matched level, ranks, gold and target defenses. Repeat against a moving opponent with a fixed incoming damage pattern. Record damage packets, missed actions, resource cost and survival separately.
Keep souls, health/mana, form, item/rune stacks, transformations and game time finite and explicitly recorded. No free full ramp or infinite scaling.
failureConditions: Enemies avoid brush or AP/health investment weakens front-line resists.
The narrow damage gain does not repay lost access, survival, wave control or allied utility.
tradeoffs: Rejected assumption: A sapling is not given Maokai personal attack on-hit effects.
Confidence: plausible. Source-compatible reasoning is not in-game validation or proof of novelty/optimality.
buyOrder: Candidate six slots: Heartsteel, Riftmaker, Blackfire Torch, Rabadon's Deathcap, Cryptbloom, Ionian Boots of Lucidity. Compare two-item checkpoints before the final six-slot test; this list is not a lane shopping order.
Keep role-appropriate starters, boots and support quest/vision obligations. If the full candidate assumes farmed income, compare it separately from support income.
coverageNotes: Only Cassiopeia Q/E and Sett W have numerical adapters. Even there, these other objectives and item/rune interactions may fall outside the model.
Proc inheritance, crit, pet hits and conditional helpers remain uncertain until observed. No completed mathematical maximum is claimed.

builds.name: Situational adaptation: Magic matchup
builds.goal: Situational adaptation for Maokai: adapt to the specified fight rather than assume one universal build
builds.hypothesis: A durable controller who starts fights with a targeted root, pushes enemies with Q and recovers through repeated Sap Magic attacks. Separate passive attack healing, melee control and brush sapling effects. Fix target position and cooldown reduction sources; AP damage must repay weaker engage durability. MR and nearby magic amplification test durable contact against magic pressure.
builds.summary: MR and nearby magic amplification test durable contact against magic pressure.
testPlan: Kit question for Maokai: Separate passive attack healing, melee control and brush sapling effects. Fix target position and cooldown reduction sources; AP damage must repay weaker engage durability.

Start with the early core (Hollow Radiance or other MR first when justified) plus appropriate boots at matched gold. Record level, actual ability ranks, forms, resource and item transformations; six-item results do not establish lane strength. Use your intended lane or jungle role; jungle starters and early consumables are outside the final six slots.

Compare against the reference route at the same level, gold spent, finite stacks and opponent setup. Record unused gold; isolate an item change before changing runes. Run three repeatable trials of a short trade and a ten-second fight. Record damage actually landed, attacks/casts, misses, remaining resource and survival. Record available/max mana and any transformed mana-item state.

Measure the actual interaction before granting item/rune procs: MR and nearby magic amplification test durable contact against magic pressure. Test once stationary, then with a moving opponent and a fixed incoming damage pattern. Choose the opponent profile this defensive route is intended to address, then repeat against the wrong damage type.

Q evidence: Maokai knocks back nearby enemies with a shockwave, dealing magic damage and slowing them. Keep finite champion/item/rune stacks explicit. Use Practice Tool, a custom match or your own replay; no numerical adapter is available for this champion.
failureConditions: MR is wasted against the wrong threat; nearby aura range and healing eligibility matter.

The route fails Maokai's stated kit question: Separate passive attack healing, melee control and brush sapling effects. Fix target position and cooldown reduction sources; AP damage must repay weaker engage durability.
Higher dummy damage is offset by fewer landed actions, deaths before the useful window, or worse ally utility.
tradeoffs: MR is wasted against the wrong threat; nearby aura range and healing eligibility matter.
Full cost 15,600 gold; delayed items, resource starvation and the two-item spike must be judged separately.
Counter-items are conditional. Change boots/defense for the real matchup, then record the modified setup.
buyOrder: Hollow Radiance or other MR first when justified. Adapt component timing to lane/jungle pressure; do not blindly follow the displayed six-item order.
Keep appropriate boots while building the early core; swap boots only when the measured matchup justifies it.
Abyssal Mask, Spirit Visage, Jak'Sho, The Protean are later or conditional slots; do not postpone necessary protection for a six-item ceiling.
Record available/max mana and any transformed mana-item state.
coverageNotes: No numerical damage or survival adapter exists for this champion. Loading this proposal opens a manual test sheet, not calculated damage.
Source formulas remain in Champion kit. Symbolic values, unresolved tokens and helper records are evidence to inspect, not a certified executable simulator.
Legal source item/rune references were checked; retained map flags cannot prove every live-shop condition. Confirm shop eligibility, exact on-hit/on-attack rules and real proc cooldowns in game.

builds.summary: Count P heals under controlled incoming spell cadence.
builds.goal: Count P heals under controlled incoming spell cadence.
builds.hypothesis: P heals from max health on the next attack and cooldown falls four seconds on ability use or enemy champion ability hits. E champion hit reduces it another four seconds; haste/resists permit real casts and Unending Despair adds close-range recovery. Iceborn gives one actual attack slow after W.
